paper_metadata.title: Quantum Data Learning of Topological-to-Ferromagnetic Phase Transitions in the 2+1D Toric Code Loop Gas Model

summary: The paper studies quantum data learning on the 2+1D toric‑code loop‑gas model using VQE-generated ground states for lattices up to 4×3 (17 qubits, 300 states per lattice). A QCNN achieves up to 100% phase-classification accuracy and estimates the critical point with finite‑size extrapolation xc(∞)=0.2518±0.026, close to the QMC benchmark xc≈0.25, while an unsupervised quantum k‑means method yields xc≈0.293. All results are obtained via classical simulation.

experiments.description: Supervised quantum data learning of the 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model using a QCNN trained on VQE-generated ground states across multiple lattice sizes, including random-split classification and physics-aware phase-boundary estimation.

algorithm.variant: quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) for phase classification

hyperparameters.physics_aware_training_window: train on x < 0.2 or x > 0.4; test on 0.2 <= x <= 0.4

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum states prepared by VQE are fed directly into the QCNN; no classical feature encoding is used.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary phase classification between topologically ordered (-1) and ferromagnetically ordered (+1) phases; decision function y_out = <Z_out> after QCNN processing.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(x) = (1 - x) H_TCM - x sum_i sigma^z_i

problem_instance.description: 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model in a magnetic field on finite open-boundary lattices; phase classification and transition-point estimation.

dataset_specification.description: Lattices 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3; 300 states per lattice; half sampled from x in [0, xc], half from x in [xc + 1e-2, 1].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Ground states generated by VQE; labels assigned using approximate critical point xc ≈ 0.25; balanced sampling across phases; physics-aware split excludes near-critical region 0.2 <= x <= 0.4 for transition estimation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Random 80/20 train-test split for classification; separate physics-aware split for phase-boundary estimation; reported accuracies and flip-interval estimates across lattice sizes.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: VQE-generated ground states used as inputs; labels derived from approximate critical point.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Phase labels and flip-interval estimators extracted from QCNN output <Z_out>; finite-size scaling fit to x'_c(L) = x_c(inf) + a / L_eff.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training loss curves shown; QCNN converges more slowly than CNN baselines

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit computational speedup is claimed; the paper reports empirical accuracy and phase-boundary estimation improvements over classical baselines.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed in the paper; experiments limited to simulated systems of up to 17 qubits with no resource estimate for scaling QCNN learning beyond classical tractability.
limiting_factors: All experiments performed in classical simulation
No asymptotic complexity comparison with classical ML
State preparation via VQE dominates cost
Classical baselines operate on full amplitudes unavailable in real experiments

notes: num_qubits reported as the smallest lattice size (2x2 -> 4 qubits); paper also studies 7, 12, and 17 qubits for larger lattices.
hardware.type not specified in the paper; inferred as not_specified.
circuit_depth not explicitly reported; QCNN is described as logarithmic-depth, but no numeric depth is given.
No asymptotic speedup claim is characterized; only empirical performance comparisons are reported.
The paper states QCNNs 'outperform classical alternatives' in estimating the phase transition but only on tiny simulated systems.
No runtime or complexity advantage is demonstrated; comparison is purely empirical on small datasets.

experiments.description: Unsupervised quantum k-means clustering on VQE-generated toric-code ground states to identify the topological-to-ferromagnetic phase boundary without labels.

algorithm.variant: quantum k-means clustering based on state overlaps / fidelities

hyperparameters.cluster_orientation: small-x states assigned to topological phase

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Direct clustering in Hilbert space using pairwise state overlaps; no classical encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize total intra-cluster distance L = sum_c sum_{i in C_c} d^2(psi_i, psi_m_c) with d(psi_i, psi_j) = sqrt(2(1 - |<psi_i|psi_j>|^2)).
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(x) = (1 - x) H_TCM - x sum_i sigma^z_i

problem_instance.description: Same toric-code loop-gas dataset as the supervised QCNN experiment; unsupervised phase clustering across lattice sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3.

dataset_specification.description: 300 VQE ground states per lattice size; balanced across phases; x sampled over [0,1] with phase labels only used for evaluation/orientation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: State fidelities computed from quantum states; cluster labels oriented so that small-x states correspond to the topological phase.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Cluster assignments analyzed as a function of x; flip-interval estimator ˆx_c extracted and compared across lattice sizes and against QMC benchmark.

implementation_details.classical_solver: quantum k-means clustering routine (classical optimization over quantum-state distances)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: VQE-generated states and pairwise fidelities used as inputs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Cluster flip-interval estimator ˆx_c extracted from cluster labels versus x; finite-size comparison to QMC.

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed; the method is presented as an unsupervised alternative that estimates the phase boundary without labels.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires scalable computation of quantum state overlaps/fidelities between many states; no resource analysis provided.
limiting_factors: Entire study performed with classical simulation
Overlap computations scale poorly with system size
No complexity comparison against classical clustering

notes: num_qubits reported as the smallest lattice size (2x2 -> 4 qubits); larger lattices use 7, 12, and 17 qubits.
hardware.type not specified in the paper; inferred as not_specified.
No circuit depth is reported for the clustering routine.
No asymptotic speedup order is characterized; only empirical comparison to QCNN and classical baselines is given.
Quantum k-means is presented as an unsupervised alternative but is not shown to outperform classical clustering methods.
Performance is similar to QCNN in locating phase boundaries but without runtime comparisons.
